content: Life is neither good or evil, but only a place for good and evil.
author: Marcus Aurelius
story:
Written in military campaign tents along the freezing Danube River during the Marcomannic Wars (170–180 CE), Marcus wrestled with the Antonine Plague, the betrayal of General Avidius Cassius, and the crushing responsibilities of the Roman Empire. In his private journal, he strictly commanded himself to master his judgments, embrace cosmic duty, and remain uncorrupted by imperial power.

In formulating this reflection, Marcus Aurelius stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of ethics. For Marcus Aurelius, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?
